score_scale: Each criterion scored 1-10. Overall = weighted mean. pass_threshold applies to the geometric-median aggregate across the panel.

criteria.name: Chiptune: authentic chip timbres, not 'chiptune-ish synth' (chiptune-8bit only)
criteria.anchor: NES Ricoh 2A03: EXACTLY five voices — 2 pulse, 1 triangle, 1 noise, 1 DPCM; no reverb on the chip, no filter; duty cycles 12.5%/25%/50% (25% = reedy classic lead; 50% = hollow square); triangle = bass (no volume control, octave lower); noise = percussion via envelope; fast frame-rate arpeggios (~60 Hz swaps) fake chords from monophony; volume is 16 steps, not fades; echo (one quiet re-triggered note) not reverb (NESdev APU wiki; musicproductionwiki chiptune; chiptune-8bit prompt craft notes). A stacked chord that rings as a chord is a hardware-impossible defect. Smooth analog pads, reverb tails, realistic instruments = OUT of genre.
criteria.evidence: pct_energy_above_8khz (noise percussion + pulse brightness read high; lush filtered pads read differently), the style prompt's timbre claims, crest_factor_db. Unverifiable specifics (duty cycle) must be marked unverifiable, not guessed.
criteria.guide: 10 = prompt claims the exact 5-voice palette + no-reverb + arp-bass pattern AND numbers consistent. 7 = palette claimed, one element unverifiable. 4 = 'retro synth' claim without the voice budget or with reverb/pads allowed. 1 = modern synth production with a chiptune label.

criteria.name: Boss/battle energy (elemental-*, epic-orchestral-boss)
criteria.anchor: Boss battle: fast tempos 130-200 BPM (typical 140-180; OoT boss 180; KH-style ~170); ostinatos and percussion are the anchors; chromaticism in chords and melody; heavy syncopation; timpani + snare militaristic layers; multi-phase feel with key changes/choir entries (Matthew Chilelli boss-battle analysis; tunee boss-battle guide: BPM range 130-200; videogamemusicshrine OoT boss analysis: 6/4, atonal/chromatic, ostinato anchors).
criteria.evidence: bpm + bpm_candidates (boss claims need a fast candidate), rms_1s_spread_db (phase evolution), duration_s, the style prompt.
criteria.guide: 10 = fast-tempo candidate + multi-phase dynamics evidence + ostinato/percussion claims. 7 = fast + energy evidence, phases unverifiable. 4 = mid-tempo (~110-130) with a boss claim. 1 = slow ambient track with a battle label.

criteria.name: Loop safety for game use (all gamer genres)
criteria.anchor: Game assets demand seamless loops: loop packs must be seamless + click-free with stated BPM/key (architecture §13); loop point ends on a phrase that leads back to bar 1; no reverb tail across the seam; loopable structure maintains intensity without sounding repetitive (tunee loopable request pattern; game-assets lane: requires stems, loop_point, seamless_loop).
criteria.evidence: Tail/head RMS compatibility for a loop (last-1s RMS within ~6 dB of first-1s RMS, no fade-to-silence on a loop claim), silences_ge_1s, bar math: duration_s * bpm / 240 should land near a whole bar count.
criteria.guide: 10 = seam-compatible levels AND whole-bar duration at the claimed BPM. 7 = levels compatible, bar math ambiguous. 4 = fade ending or fractional-bar duration. 1 = hard truncation/seam click evidence.

criteria.name: Asset-pack packaging (stems, BPM/key metadata, naming)
criteria.anchor: Game-asset lane requires: stems, loop_point, seamless_loop, metadata (lanes.yaml game-assets). Asset-pack packaging: loops must state BPM and key, stems time-aligned, clean WAV, consistent naming (architecture §13). Indie devs buy asset packs at $2,500-7,500 for 5-10 tracks.
criteria.evidence: Package contents and manifest fields when present.
criteria.guide: 10 = stems + BPM/key + loop-point marker present. 7 = master + metadata. 4 = bare master. 1 = nothing.

criteria.name: Master hits the lane loudness target
criteria.anchor: Streaming -14 LUFS; game-asset delivery favours consistent loudness with real dynamics (boss cues need wide dynamic range — 'quiet dread to full assault', tunee).
criteria.guide: 10 = within +/-1 dB. 7 = within +/-3 dB. 4 = 3-6 dB off. 1 = 6+ dB off.

reject_signals: chiptune claim with reverb/pads/realistic instruments or >2-note chords per channel (hardware-impossible = OUT of genre)
boss/battle claim with no fast-tempo candidate (under 130 BPM)
fade-out or truncated ending on a game-loop claim
no stated BPM/key for a game-asset product

sources.title: How to Recreate the Chiptune Sound (8-Bit / NES)
Writing a Boss Battle Track - Matthew Chilelli
Inside The Score: Zelda OoT Boss Battle

notes: Two sub-idioms live in this family: chip (hardware-constraint timbre) and orchestral battle (tempo/ostinato/phase). elemental-* tracks choose per their prompt; chiptune-8bit MUST pass chip_timbre_authenticity; battle tracks MUST pass battle_energy. Loop safety is common to all game-asset delivery.
